parole.significato: Any of the divisions of the eighth circle of Hell, Malebolge, in Dante's Divine Comedy.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Italian bolgia (“ditch, trench”), from Old French bolge, bouge, from Late Latin bulga (“wallet, purse”), from Gaulish bolgā, from Proto-Celtic *bolgos (“sack, bag”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵʰ- (“to swell”). Doublet of budge and bulge.

parole.significato: A genre of Italian cinema mixing mystery and thriller with psychological elements.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian giallo (literally “yellow”), in reference to the yellow covers of a series of mystery novels published by Mondadori from 1929.

parole.significato: A roofed, open gallery, usually on an upper level.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian loggia, from Old French loge, from Medieval Latin laubĭa, from Frankish *laubijā. Doublet of lobby and lodge.
From Italian mangiare (“to eat”), from Old French mangier (“to eat”), from Latin mandūcāre (“to eat”). Doublet of mungaree.

parole.significato: Any coastal area popular with tourists.
parole.testo: From Italian riviera, from Old French riviere, from Latin riparius. Doublet of river and rivière.
